question.problem:
Compute $P(3<X<4)$ given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{x}^{2},\, & -1\le x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{9}(x-1) & 1<x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
If a continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x),$ then 

$$
P(a<X<b)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, in our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3<X<4) & ={\int }_{3}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{1}{9}(x-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-x]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}([\frac{1}{2}(4)^{2}-(4)]-[\frac{1}{2}(3)^{2}-(3)]) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(8-4-\frac{9}{2}+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}(\frac{5}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
